#### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Load packages

```{r setup}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)   
tidymodels_prefer()   
```


#### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Data exploration and formatting

```{r}
#| message: false

default_data <- read_csv("default_data.csv")   # load dataset

glimpse(default_data)   # observe variable types

```


```{r}
# convert character types to factor types

# keep the natural order (No, Yes)

# glm() models the probability of the SECOND level, so the coefficients
# describe the log-odds of default = "Yes" (same as on the slides)

# yardstick treats the FIRST level as the event by default, so every
# metric call below needs event_level = "second"

default_data <- default_data |>
  mutate(default = factor(default, levels =  c("No", "Yes")),
         student = factor(student))

glimpse(default_data)

```


```{r}

levels(default_data$default)   # "Yes" is the second level = the event

```


```{r}
# overall class frequency and proportion

default_data |>
  count(default) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n))

```


#### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Data splitting

```{r}
# data splitting (stratified, so both sets keep the ~3% default rate)

set.seed(208)

default_split <- initial_split(default_data, prop = 0.8, strata = default)

default_train <- training(default_split)   # training set

default_test <- testing(default_split)     # test set

```


```{r}
# class frequencies and proportions

# training set
default_train |>
  count(default) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n))

# test set
default_test |>
  count(default) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n))

```


#### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Logistic Regression - Model training

```{r}
# write the recipe

default_recipe <- recipe(default ~ balance, data = default_train) 

```


```{r}
# specify the model, package engine, task/mode

logreg_spec <- logistic_reg() |>
  set_engine("glm") |> 
  set_mode("classification")

logreg_spec

```


```{r}
# workflow = recipe + model

logreg_wflow <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(default_recipe) |>
  add_model(logreg_spec)

logreg_wflow

```


```{r}
# fit the model on the training set

logreg_fit <- logreg_wflow |>
  fit(data = default_train)

logreg_fit

```


```{r}
#| fig-align: "center"
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4

# the fitted S-shaped curve stays between 0 and 1
# only for visualizing the model and for demonstration

balance_grid <- tibble(balance = seq(min(default_train$balance), max(default_train$balance), by = 10))

augment(logreg_fit, new_data = balance_grid) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = balance, y = .pred_Yes)) +
  geom_point(data = default_train,
             aes(x = balance, y = as.numeric(default == "Yes")),
             alpha = 0.1, color = "orange") +
  geom_line(color = "blue", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "Balance", y = "Predicted probability of default")

```


#### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Obtaining predictions 

```{r}
# predicted probability of default for balance = $700 (for one observation)

predict(logreg_fit, new_data = tibble(balance = 700), type = "prob")

```


```{r}
# predictions for the entire test set
# augment() adds .pred_class, .pred_No, .pred_Yes to the test set in one step

default_test_preds <- augment(logreg_fit, new_data = default_test)

default_test_preds |>
  # select(default, balance, .pred_class, .pred_No, .pred_Yes) |>   # optional
  head(10)

```


```{r}
# class predictions with a threshold we choose ourselves

threshold <- 0.2   # set threshold

default_test_preds <- default_test_preds |>
  mutate(.pred_class_thresh = factor(if_else(.pred_Yes > threshold, "Yes", "No"),
                                     levels = c("No", "Yes")))


default_test_preds

```


#### ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Model Assessment

### confusion matrix

```{r}
# create confusion matrix (rows = predicted, columns = actual)

logreg_cm <- default_test_preds |>
  conf_mat(truth = default, estimate = .pred_class)

logreg_cm

```


```{r}
# all metrics at once
# NOTE the event_level = "second" which is class "Yes"

summary(logreg_cm, event_level = "second")

```


### ROC curve and AUC

```{r}
#| fig-align: "center"
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 6

# ROC curve

logreg_roc <- default_test_preds |>
  roc_curve(truth = default, .pred_Yes, event_level = "second")

autoplot(logreg_roc)

```


```{r}
# obtain AUC

default_test_preds |>
  roc_auc(truth = default, .pred_Yes, event_level = "second")

```
